q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The remark 'said to contain' endorsed on a Railway Receipt signifies that the goods were packed and loaded by the consignor and their contents were not checked by the railway staff.
2. The endorsement 'sender's weight accepted' on a Railway Receipt indicates that the weight declared by the consignor has been accepted for booking as no weighbridge is available at the forwarding station, subject to weighment en route or at destination.
e: The remark said to contain means the consignor packed and loaded the goods and railway staff did not check the contents, and sender's weight accepted means the declared weight was accepted where no weighbridge exists, subject to later weighment, so both are correct.

q: A consignment is delivered at the destination station short of the booked quantity or weight. To support his claim for compensation, the consignee should obtain from the destination station:

options.A: A damage certificate for the consignment
options.B: An error sheet issued by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: An overcharge sheet for refund of the freight
options.D: A shortage certificate recording the short delivery of the consignment

e: For a short delivery the consignee should obtain a shortage certificate from the destination station recording the quantity or weight delivered short, to support his compensation claim.

q: A company is permitted to lay a pipeline across railway land on payment of charges to the Railways. Such charges recovered by the Railways are known as:
e: Charges for permission to lay a pipeline across railway land are way leave charges, recovered for the facility of way leave over railway land.

q: A consignment has arrived at the destination station, but the freight and all other charges due in respect of it remain unpaid. Under the Railways Act, the railway administration may:

options.A: Sell the consignment by public auction immediately on its arrival
options.B: Detain the consignment and exercise a lien on it until the freight and all other charges due in respect of it are paid
options.C: Release the consignment without payment and recover the dues from the forwarding station
options.D: Return the consignment to the consignor at the cost of the Railways

e: Under the Railways Act the railway administration has a lien on a consignment for unpaid freight and other charges and may detain it until those dues are paid.

q: Before the reservation chart is prepared, a passenger reports that his confirmed reserved ticket has been lost. In this situation, a duplicate ticket may be issued to him:

options.A: Free of charge in all cases
options.B: Only after the journey is completed
options.C: On recovery of the prescribed charges, subject to the conditions laid down in the Coaching Tariff
options.D: Only at the destination station of the journey

e: A duplicate ticket for a lost confirmed reserved ticket reported before chart preparation is issued on recovery of the prescribed charges, subject to the conditions in the Coaching Tariff.

q: After all efforts at recovery have failed, a debit standing against a station is found to be irrecoverable. Such an amount can be written off only:

options.A: By the Station Master at the end of the month
options.B: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection of the station
options.C: By adjustment against the earnings of the following month
options.D: Under the sanction of the competent authority, with the concurrence of the Finance or Accounts branch

e: An irrecoverable station debit can be written off only under sanction of the competent authority with the concurrence of Finance or Accounts; neither the Station Master nor the Travelling Inspector of Accounts can do so.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Inland Container Depots (ICDs) operated by CONCOR are dry ports where export and import containers are handled and customs formalities are completed away from the seaports.
2. In container traffic, 'EXIM' containers are those which carry export and import traffic between the gateway ports and the inland container depots.
e: CONCOR's Inland Container Depots are dry ports handling export and import containers with customs formalities away from seaports, and EXIM containers carry that export-import traffic between gateway ports and ICDs, so both are correct.

q: On a running train, the Travelling Ticket Examiner carries a Hand Held Terminal (HHT). The terminal enables him to:

options.A: Issue unreserved tickets to passengers at stations
options.B: Print the reservation charts at the starting station
options.C: Check the tickets of passengers and allot vacant berths on the train, the data being synchronised with the reservation system
options.D: Collect freight from goods customers dealt with en route

e: The Hand Held Terminal with the Travelling Ticket Examiner syncs with the reservation system, enabling him to check tickets and allot vacant berths on the running train.

q:
Consider the following statements about the inspection of a station by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts:
1. He verifies the cash balance of the station with the balance shown in the station accounts and reports any discrepancy.
2. He also verifies the physical stock of tickets and money-value books of the station with the ticket stock register of the station.
e: On station inspection the Travelling Inspector of Accounts verifies the station cash balance against the accounts and the physical stock of tickets and money-value books against the ticket stock register, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statutory audit of station accounts is exercised by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts.
2. Statutory audit of railway accounts, including station accounts, is exercised by the Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
e: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts exercises internal check, not statutory audit; statutory audit of railway accounts is by the Railway Audit organisation under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about the check exercised in the Traffic Accounts Office:
1. Parcel Way Bills rendered by stations are checked primarily to ensure that the parcel charges have been correctly levied in accordance with the scales in force and duly brought to account.
2. The goods invoices rendered by forwarding stations are checked with a view to verifying, among other things, the correctness of the classification, chargeable weight and freight charged on the consignments.
e: Traffic Accounts check of Parcel Way Bills verifies that parcel charges are correctly levied per the scales in force and brought to account, and goods invoices are checked for classification, chargeable weight and freight, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about the apportionment of the earnings of through traffic among the zonal railways:
1. Such apportionment continues to be necessary principally because each zonal railway is a separate accounting unit whose earnings and financial results are assessed separately.
2. Apportionment has the effect of merely distributing the through earnings among the railways concerned, without altering the total earnings of Indian Railways as a whole.
e: Apportionment of through earnings remains necessary because each zonal railway is a separate accounting unit assessed separately, and it only distributes the total among railways without changing the all-India total, so both are correct.

q: 'Smalls' traffic, that is, consignments which do not make up a full wagon load, is charged for carriage:

options.B: Free of charge up to the prescribed minimum weight
options.C: At a scale of rates which is higher per unit of weight than the wagonload scale, in view of the higher cost of handling such traffic
options.D: At parcel rates in all cases

e: Smalls, being less than a wagon load, bear a higher scale per unit weight than wagonload traffic because of their higher handling cost, and are not charged at trainload or parcel rates.

q: A consignment is light but bulky, occupying space disproportionate to its actual weight. Freight on such a consignment is charged:

options.A: Only on its actual weight in all cases
options.B: At double the normal freight in all cases
options.C: Only when the consignment is booked at railway risk
options.D: On the basis of measurement weight, computed from the dimensions of the packages at the prescribed conversion

e: A light but bulky consignment is charged on measurement weight, computed from the dimensions of the packages at the prescribed conversion, instead of its lower actual weight.

q: A consignor offers a consignment whose dimensions infringe the standard moving dimensions. Such an Over Dimensional Consignment can be accepted for carriage:

options.A: Only with prior sanction and subject to special conditions and charges
options.C: Only in wagons owned by the consignor himself

e: An Over Dimensional Consignment infringing standard moving dimensions can be accepted only with prior sanction and subject to special conditions and charges governing its safe movement.

q: Under the e-payment system for freight, the arrangement works on the basis that:

options.A: The freight is first collected in cash at the goods shed and is reimbursed to the Railways by the bank later
options.B: It works under a tripartite agreement among the Railways, the bank and the freight customer, under which the freight is debited directly to the customer's bank account
options.C: The freight is paid by the customer by money order to the destination station
options.D: The freight is collected by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection

e: Freight e-payment works under a tripartite agreement among the Railways, the bank and the freight customer, under which freight is debited directly to the customer's bank account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under a Privilege Ticket Order (PTO), a railway employee, with his family where admissible, can travel on payment of one-third of the public fare.
2. A railway employee travelling on a Privilege Pass is required to pay no fare, the pass itself entitling him to free travel.
e: A Privilege Ticket Order entitles the employee and admissible family to travel on payment of one-third of the public fare, while a Privilege Pass itself entitles free travel with no fare payable, so both are correct.

q: Certain berths in a train are kept apart and are released only under the orders of the competent authority, in favour of high officials and persons in urgent need of travel. This earmarked accommodation is known as the:

options.B: Emergency Quota, commonly called the HO quota

e: Accommodation released only under orders of the competent authority for high officials and urgent need is the Emergency Quota, commonly called the HO quota.

q: To help passengers who find upper berths difficult to use, a quota of lower berths in trains is earmarked for allotment, subject to availability and the conditions prescribed, to:

options.A: Season ticket holders travelling on the section
options.D: Senior citizens, female passengers and pregnant women

e: A lower berth quota is earmarked, subject to availability and prescribed conditions, for senior citizens, female passengers and pregnant women who find upper berths difficult to use.

q: A passenger holding a through journey ticket breaks his journey at an intermediate station. For the break of journey so availed of to be regular, he is required to:

options.A: Purchase a fresh ticket from the station of break for the rest of the journey in all cases
options.B: Get his ticket endorsed by the station staff at the station where the journey is broken
options.C: Surrender his ticket at the station of break and claim a refund of the fare
options.D: Obtain the prior permission of the Railway Board for the break of journey

e: A break of journey on a through ticket is regular only when the ticket is endorsed by the station staff at the station where the journey is broken.

q: A station receives rent for railway quarters let out to outsiders, which is classified as a sundry other earning. In the classification of earnings of the Railways, sundry other earnings are booked under:
e: In the classification of railway earnings, sundry other earnings such as rent of quarters let to outsiders are booked under Abstract X, while coaching and goods earnings have their own abstracts.

q: A station remits its earnings to the bank on the last day of a month, but the amount is not credited to the Railways' account by the close of that month. In the accounts, this amount is carried as:
e: Earnings remitted by a station but not credited by the bank by month end are carried as Cash-in-Transit, representing remittances in transit to the Railways' account.

q:
Consider the following statements about Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC):
1. At the time of preparation of the reservation chart, RAC passengers are provided confirmed accommodation against the berths falling vacant through cancellations, in the order of their RAC priority.
2. Under the RAC arrangement, two passengers are allotted one side-lower berth to share for sitting.
e: At charting, RAC passengers get confirmed berths against cancellations in RAC priority order, and pending confirmation two RAC passengers share one side-lower berth for sitting, so both statements are correct.

q: A passenger presents a reserved ticket which is torn and mutilated, and claims refund of the fare at the station. Refund in such a case is admissible at the station if:

options.A: The passenger produces a fresh ticket for the same journey
options.B: The ticket is countersigned by the Station Master
options.C: The particulars of the ticket, such as the ticket number and the PNR number, are clearly legible
options.D: The passenger surrenders his identity proof along with the ticket

e: Refund on a torn and mutilated ticket is admissible at the station only if its particulars, such as the ticket number and PNR number, are clearly legible for verification.

q: A station has to make a petty official payment which is required to be made at the station itself. Such a payment is met:

options.A: Out of the traffic earnings collected at the station, without any separate authority
options.B: By the Traffic Accounts Office through a pay order
options.C: By raising a debit against another station of the section
options.D: From the cash imprest held at the station for the purpose, which is recouped on rendering the paid vouchers

e: Petty official payments at a station are met from the station cash imprest held for the purpose, which is recouped on rendering the paid vouchers.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989 deals with fraudulently travelling or attempting to travel without a proper pass or ticket.
2. Under Section 142 of the Railways Act, 1989, transfer of a ticket or of reserved accommodation by a person other than an authorised railway servant or agent is prohibited and punishable.
e: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989 covers fraudulently travelling without a proper pass or ticket, and Section 142 prohibits and punishes transfer of tickets or reserved accommodation by unauthorised persons, so both are correct.

q: A passenger has booked a reserved ticket at a computerised reservation counter in one city and later wishes to cancel it at a reservation counter in another city. The correct position is that the ticket:

options.A: Can be cancelled only at the counter at which it was booked
options.B: Can be cancelled at any computerised reservation counter, and not necessarily at the counter or station of booking
options.C: Cannot be cancelled at all once it is printed
options.D: Can be cancelled only through the Railway Claims Tribunal

e: A computerised reservation ticket can be cancelled at any computerised reservation counter, not necessarily the counter or station of booking, since the reservation system is networked.

q: 'Gross receipts' of the Railways, as distinct from their 'gross earnings', also take into account:

options.A: The capital expenditure incurred during the period
options.B: The appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: The suspense accounts connected with traffic transactions
options.D: The dividend payable to General Revenues

e: Gross receipts, unlike gross earnings, also take into account the suspense accounts connected with traffic transactions, that is amounts under Traffic Suspense awaiting final adjustment.

q: Immediately after a train accident, an ex gratia payment is made to a victim. In regard to this payment, the correct position is that it is:

options.A: The final compensation for the accident, in full and final settlement of the claim
options.B: A loan to the victim, recoverable from him in monthly instalments
options.C: Payable only after the Railway Claims Tribunal passes its final order
options.D: An immediate ad-hoc relief, which is adjusted against the compensation finally awarded

e: Ex gratia payment after an accident is immediate ad-hoc relief to the victim; it is not final compensation and is adjusted against the compensation finally awarded.

q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of goods for freight rating:
1. The classification is based mainly on the principle of charging what the traffic can bear.
2. The classification of commodities for the purpose of goods freight rating is issued by the Indian Railway Conference Association.
e: Goods classification rests mainly on charging what the traffic can bear, and the classification of commodities for freight rating is issued by the Indian Railway Conference Association, so both statements are correct.

q: A consignor books a consignment but gives no instructions about the route by which it is to be carried. In such a case, the freight on the consignment is charged on the basis of the distance by:

options.A: The longest route available between the two stations
options.C: The route by which the consignment is actually carried, even if it is the longest
options.D: The average of the distances by all the available routes

e: Where the consignor gives no route instructions, freight is charged on the distance by the shortest, that is cheapest, route between the forwarding and destination stations.

q: After the goods invoices rendered by forwarding stations have been checked in the Traffic Accounts Office, the Machine Prepared Abstracts are:

options.A: Destroyed along with the invoices checked
options.B: Returned to the consignors for their record
options.C: Printed destination station-wise and sent to the stations concerned
options.D: Sent to the Railway Board for apportionment of earnings

e: After check of goods invoices, Machine Prepared Abstracts are printed destination station-wise and sent to the stations concerned for their accounts and apportionment purposes.

q: A passenger objects to another passenger smoking in the compartment of a train. Under Section 167 of the Railways Act, 1989, the position is that smoking in the compartment is prohibited where:

options.A: The train is running at night
options.B: The compartment is an air-conditioned coach
options.C: The passenger holds only an unreserved ticket
options.D: Any other passenger in the compartment objects to the smoking

e: Section 167 of the Railways Act, 1989 prohibits smoking in a compartment if any other passenger in the compartment objects to it.

q:
Consider the following statements about the electronic Railway Receipt under the Freight Operations Information System:
1. The Railway Receipt for a consignment is generated electronically by the system on capture of the booking particulars.
2. A consignee holding an electronic Railway Receipt can take delivery of his consignment by using the e-surrender facility, by which the electronic Railway Receipt is surrendered online for delivery.
e: Under the Freight Operations Information System the Railway Receipt is generated electronically on capture of booking particulars, and the consignee can take delivery by e-surrender of the electronic Railway Receipt online, so both are correct.

q: A consignment has been delivered at a station and the consignee now wants to remove the goods from the station premises. Before the goods are so removed:

options.A: A fresh Railway Receipt is issued to the consignee
options.B: The delivery is recorded in the delivery book and a gate pass is issued for their removal
options.C: The consignment is re-weighed in the presence of the consignee
options.D: A debit is raised against the forwarding station

e: Before goods are removed from station premises after delivery, the delivery is recorded in the delivery book and a gate pass is issued authorising their removal.

q: During the check of a goods invoice, an official in the Traffic Accounts Office has to verify the correctness of the distance for which freight has been charged. This is verified with reference to:

options.B: The passenger classification return of the station
options.C: The Local Distance Tables and the Junction Distance Tables in force
options.D: The Machine Prepared Abstract of the destination station

e: The distance charged on a goods invoice is verified in the Traffic Accounts Office with reference to the Local Distance Tables and Junction Distance Tables in force.

q: The passenger classification return rendered by a station shows, among other things:

options.A: Only the total number of passengers booked from the station during the month
options.B: The names of the passengers who travelled on concession tickets
options.C: The commencing number of tickets only, the closing number being shown in the goods returns
options.D: The commencing and closing numbers of tickets, the index numbers of non-issued tickets and the amounts derived from full-fare tickets and concession tickets

e: The passenger classification return shows the commencing and closing numbers of tickets, index numbers of non-issued tickets, and amounts from full-fare and concession tickets, not merely the passenger count.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Coaching earnings of through traffic are apportioned among the railways in proportion to the distance travelled over each railway.
2. Vehicle kilometres are counted only for the distance run by coaches while carrying passengers.
e: Coaching earnings of through traffic are apportioned among railways in proportion to distance travelled over each, but vehicle kilometres are counted for all running of coaches and not only while carrying passengers, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A person who has applied for compensation for a train accident desires immediate relief pending the determination of his claim. Under Section 126 of the Railways Act, 1989, such interim relief is paid by:

options.A: The railway administration, pending determination of the compensation by the Claims Tribunal
options.B: The Railway Claims Tribunal, out of its own funds
options.C: The State Government of the place where the accident occurred
options.D: The insurance company with which the passenger is insured

e: Under Section 126 of the Railways Act, 1989 interim relief pending determination of an accident compensation claim is paid by the railway administration, not by the Tribunal or any insurer.

q: A station clerk is preparing the monthly Station Balance Sheet of his station. Which of the following items should he NOT enter in it?

options.A: 'To-pay' freight which has not yet been collected
options.B: The value of the stores held in the station godown
options.C: Wharfage and demurrage which have accrued but have not yet been realised
options.D: Remittances made by the station during the month

e: The Station Balance Sheet covers traffic transactions such as to-pay freight, accrued wharfage and demurrage and remittances; the value of stores held in the station godown is not a traffic item and is not entered in it.

q: A Travelling Inspector of Accounts takes up the inspection of a station whose accounts of the past several months are due for check. The extent of check ordinarily exercised by him at such an inspection is:

options.A: A complete check of the accounts of all the months since the last inspection
options.B: No check of accounts at all, his inspection being confined to the cash balance
options.C: A complete check of the accounts of one selected month and a test check of the accounts of the other months
options.D: A check only of the goods accounts, the coaching accounts being checked in the Traffic Accounts Office

e: A Travelling Inspector of Accounts ordinarily exercises a complete check of the accounts of one selected month and a test check of the accounts of the other months since the last inspection.

q: In regard to the Accounts Office Balance Sheet, the correct position is that it is:

options.A: A copy of the Station Balance Sheet rendered by the station, reproduced in the Traffic Accounts Office
options.B: Prepared by the station and merely countersigned in the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: Compiled by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection
options.D: Compiled independently in the Traffic Accounts Office from its own books and records

e: The Accounts Office Balance Sheet is compiled independently in the Traffic Accounts Office from its own books and records, not copied or countersigned from the Station Balance Sheet.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Commissioner of Railway Safety:
1. A statutory inquiry into a serious train accident on the Railways is conducted by the Commissioner of Railway Safety.
2. The Commissioner of Railway Safety functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
e: A statutory inquiry into a serious train accident is conducted by the Commissioner of Railway Safety, who functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, so both statements are correct.

q: A goods train is worked over a section with the help of an assisting (banking) engine in addition to the train engine. In such a case:

options.A: The train kilometres exceed the train engine kilometres
options.B: The train engine kilometres exceed the train kilometres
options.C: The train engine kilometres are exactly equal to the train kilometres
options.D: The light engine kilometres exceed the train kilometres

e: Train engine kilometres count every engine running with the train, so with a train engine plus a banking engine they exceed the train kilometres, which count the train's run only once.

q: The actual weight of a consignment is less than the minimum weight condition prescribed for the wagon and class of traffic in which it is booked. The freight on the consignment is charged on:

options.A: The actual weight of the consignment only
options.B: Half of the minimum weight condition prescribed
options.C: The minimum weight condition prescribed, the chargeable weight being the higher of the actual weight and that condition
options.D: The carrying capacity of the wagon in all cases

e: Where actual weight is below the prescribed minimum weight condition, freight is charged on that minimum weight condition, the chargeable weight being the higher of actual weight and the condition.

q: A printed card ticket, as distinct from a ticket issued under the Unreserved Ticketing System, is:

options.A: Generated and printed on demand for the destination asked for by the passenger
options.B: Issued only through the UTS mobile application
options.C: A paperless ticket shown on the passenger's mobile phone
options.D: Pre-printed for a fixed pair of origin and destination stations

e: A printed card ticket is pre-printed for a fixed pair of origin and destination stations, unlike a UTS ticket generated on demand for the destination asked for.

q:
Consider the following statements about Automatic Ticket Vending Machines at stations:
1. The tickets sold through the machines installed at a station are accounted for in the accounts of that station.
2. The sales through the machines are made with the assistance of 'facilitators', who are paid a commission on the tickets sold through them.
e: ATVM tickets sold at a station are accounted for in that station's accounts, and facilitators assisting the sales are paid a commission on the tickets sold through them, so both statements are correct.

q: Monthly Statistical Statement 5-B of Indian Railways relates to:
e: Monthly Statistical Statement 5-B of Indian Railways relates to lubricating oil statistics, the companion fuel and power series being covered by the other parts of Statement 5.

q: Waitlisted tickets are NOT issued to passengers in:
e: Waitlisted tickets are not issued in Suvidha trains, whose accommodation is allotted only as confirmed or RAC under its dynamic pricing scheme, unlike Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Mail or Express trains.

q: Compensation paid by the Railways for loss of, or damage to, goods is accounted for by:

options.A: Deduction from the goods earnings of the Railways
options.B: Deduction from the coaching earnings of the Railways
options.C: Adjustment against the sale proceeds of unclaimed consignments
options.D: Being charged to the working expenses of the Railways, and not by deduction from the earnings

e: Compensation for loss of or damage to goods is charged to the working expenses of the Railways; it is not accounted for by deduction from goods or coaching earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The train hours used in computing the average speed of trains include the time of halts at the intermediate stations en route.
2. Train engine kilometres are always exactly equal to the train kilometres.
e: Average speed is computed from train hours that include halts at intermediate stations en route. Train engine kilometres are not always equal to train kilometres, because light engines, assisting engines and shunting add engine kilometres beyond train kilometres.

q: The reservation chart of a train has been prepared, but some accommodation in the train is still vacant. This vacant accommodation can be booked at stations as:
e: After the reservation chart is prepared, accommodation still vacant in the train is available for booking at stations as current booking, up to the departure of the train.

q: A passenger requests reservation in a train and class in which the maximum prescribed waitlist limit has already been reached. His request for reservation is declined with the status shown as:
e: When the prescribed maximum waitlist limit for a train and class is already reached, a further reservation request is declined and the status is shown as REGRET in the Passenger Reservation System.

q: The operating statistics of Indian Railways deal with:

options.A: Only the earnings of the Railways during the period
options.B: Only the expenditure of the Railways during the period
options.C: The audit objections raised on the accounts of the Railways
options.D: Physical units of performance, such as train kilometres, Net Tonne Kilometres and wagon days

e: Operating statistics are physical performance units, not money figures: they cover train kilometres, Net Tonne Kilometres, wagon days and similar measures of the work done and the use made of assets.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The gross earnings of the Railways comprise the coaching, goods and sundry other earnings accrued during the period.
2. The sale proceeds of unserviceable and surplus assets form part of the gross traffic earnings of a railway.
e: Gross earnings comprise coaching, goods and sundry other earnings accrued in the period. Sale proceeds of unserviceable and surplus assets are capital or miscellaneous receipts, not gross traffic earnings, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Under Section 49 of the Railways Act, 1989, every railway administration is required to exhibit at every station of the railway:

options.A: The list of licensed porters engaged at the station
options.B: A table of the times of arrival and departure of trains and a list of fares payable for travel from the station
options.C: The balance sheet of the station for the previous month
options.D: The names of the officials authorised to grant concessions in fares

e: Section 49 of the Railways Act, 1989 requires every railway administration to exhibit at every station a table of train arrival and departure times and a list of fares payable for travel from that station.

q: The Advice of Internal Check issued to a station conveys to it:

options.A: The individual errors and discrepancies detected in its accounts, item by item
options.B: The orders of the competent authority waiving the demurrage accrued at the station
options.C: The particulars of the tickets supplied to the station against its indent
options.D: The consolidated result — the debits and credits — of the internal check of its accounts for the month

e: The Advice of Internal Check conveys the consolidated result of the internal check of a station's accounts for the month, that is the net debits and credits to be taken to account, as distinct from the error sheet which lists individual errors.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sundry other earnings are apportioned among the zonal railways on the basis of the distance over which the traffic is carried.
2. Lease charges recovered from private operators for leasing of parcel space in brake and luggage vans and parcel vans form part of parcel earnings, classified under Other Coaching Earnings.
e: Sundry other earnings are credited to the railway on which they arise and are not apportioned on a distance basis. Lease charges for parcel space leased in brake and luggage vans and parcel vans are parcel earnings under Other Coaching Earnings, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about Tatkal tickets:
1. A passenger travelling on a Tatkal ticket is required to carry and produce one of the prescribed original photo identity proofs during the journey.
2. No concession in fare is admissible on Tatkal tickets.
e: Both statements are correct: a Tatkal passenger must carry one of the prescribed original photo identity proofs during the journey, and no concession in fare is admissible on Tatkal tickets.

q: A consignor declares the value of his consignment in excess of the prescribed limit and books the goods at railway risk. The percentage charge levied in this connection is charged:

options.A: On the weight of the consignment, at the rate prescribed per quintal
options.B: As a flat charge per Railway Receipt, irrespective of the value declared
options.C: On the freight payable on the consignment
options.D: On the value declared by the consignor in excess of the prescribed limit, towards the enhanced liability of the Railways

e: Where the declared value exceeds the prescribed limit and goods are booked at railway risk, the percentage charge is levied on the value declared in excess of that limit, as consideration for the Railways' enhanced liability.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway are confined to the traffic which originates on that railway.
2. For compiling passenger statistics, the journeys performed on season tickets are accounted for by estimating the number of journeys on a prescribed standard basis, as the actual journeys made by each holder are not recorded.
e: Net Tonne Kilometres cover all traffic moved over a railway, including through traffic, not only traffic originating on it. Season ticket journeys are not individually recorded, so passenger statistics estimate them on a prescribed standard basis; only statement 2 is correct.

q: Goods booked at the owner's risk rate are damaged in transit and the claimant seeks compensation from the Railways. In regard to the liability of the Railways, the correct position is that the railway administration is not liable unless:

options.A: The consignment was also insured by the consignor with an insurance company
options.B: The damage is certified by the Station Master of the forwarding station
options.C: The claimant had paid the percentage charge on the declared value
options.D: Negligence or misconduct on the part of the Railways or of their servants is proved by the claimant

e: For goods booked at owner's risk rate, Section 97 of the Railways Act, 1989 relieves the railway administration of liability for loss or damage unless negligence or misconduct on the part of the Railways or their servants is proved.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Station outstandings are automatically extinguished at the close of the financial year, whether they are recovered or not.
2. The outstandings under Traffic Suspense are reviewed periodically, item-wise and age-wise, to pursue their clearance.
e: Station outstandings are not extinguished at the close of the financial year; they are carried forward. Outstandings under Traffic Suspense are reviewed periodically, item-wise and age-wise, to pursue clearance, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tickets which are spoiled or cancelled before issue are destroyed at the station itself and are not required to be accounted for.
2. The used foils of Railway Receipts are destroyed at the station without any check.
e: Neither statement is correct: spoiled or cancelled tickets must still be accounted for and dealt with as prescribed, and used foils of Railway Receipts are retained and checked, not destroyed at the station without check.

q:
Consider the following statements about the facilities available to freight customers through the Freight Operations Information System:
1. Accrued demurrage and other terminal charges can be paid electronically through the e-payment facility linked with the system, without visiting the goods office.
2. Registration of demand for wagons (indents) can be made electronically through the e-demand facility of the system.
e: Both are facilities of the Freight Operations Information System: demurrage and terminal charges can be paid electronically through e-payment, and wagon demands (indents) can be registered electronically through e-demand registration.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In traffic costing, line haul cost is the cost of hauling traffic between terminals, excluding the costs incurred at the terminals themselves.
2. In traffic costing, terminal cost is the cost incurred at the originating and destination terminals in handling the traffic, such as loading, unloading and documentation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both definitions are correct: line haul cost is the cost of hauling traffic between terminals, excluding terminal costs, and terminal cost is the cost of handling traffic at the originating and destination terminals.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fully distributed cost allocates the fixed and overhead costs also to the individual services.
2. The avoidable cost of a traffic service is the cost which would be saved if that service were withdrawn or discontinued.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: fully distributed cost loads fixed and overhead costs also on individual services, and avoidable cost is the cost that would be saved if the service were withdrawn.

q: A costing officer has to divide the costs that are common to the coaching and the goods services between the two services. Under traffic costing, this apportionment is made:

options.A: Equally, in the ratio of fifty-fifty in all cases
options.C: On the basis of suitable statistical units, such as Gross Tonne Kilometres and train kilometres
options.D: On the basis of the number of staff employed in each service

e: Costs common to coaching and goods services are apportioned between them on the basis of suitable statistical units such as Gross Tonne Kilometres and train kilometres, which reflect the use made of the common facilities.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The average net load of goods trains is worked out by dividing the Net Tonne Kilometres by the goods train kilometres.
2. The average gross load of goods trains is worked out by dividing the Gross Tonne Kilometres by the goods train kilometres.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are standard statistical ratios: average net load = Net Tonne Kilometres divided by goods train kilometres, and average gross load = Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by goods train kilometres.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day is an index of locomotive output and utilisation on goods services.
2. Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day measures the gross hauling output obtained per locomotive day.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both ratios are locomotive utilisation indices: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day measures net output per locomotive day on goods services, and Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day measures the gross hauling output per locomotive day.

q: During a review, it is noticed that the Specific Fuel Consumption of a railway's locomotives has fallen over the period, other things remaining the same. This fall indicates:

options.A: A deterioration in the fuel efficiency of the locomotives
options.B: An improvement in fuel efficiency, as less fuel is consumed per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.C: An increase in the Gross Tonne Kilometres performed
options.D: A reduction in the number of locomotives in use

e: Specific Fuel Consumption is fuel consumed per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. A fall in it means less fuel is used for the same output, which indicates improved fuel efficiency.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The wagon turn-round includes the time spent by a wagon at terminals for loading, unloading and marshalling.
2. A lower wagon turn-round figure points to better utilisation of the wagon fleet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: wagon turn-round is the time from one loading to the next, including time at terminals for loading, unloading and marshalling, and a lower turn-round means wagons are cycled faster, that is better utilisation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Train kilometres per route kilometre on a section indicate the density or intensity of the train services operated on the section.
2. The density of passenger traffic on a section is expressed as passenger kilometres per route kilometre.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are density measures: train kilometres per route kilometre show the intensity of train services on a section, and passenger kilometres per route kilometre express the density of passenger traffic on it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The average number of passengers carried per train is worked out by dividing the passenger kilometres by the passenger train kilometres.
2. The average number of coaches per passenger train is worked out by dividing the vehicle kilometres by the passenger train kilometres.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: average passengers per train = passenger kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres, and average coaches per passenger train = vehicle kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres.

q: An operating officer uses the index 'wagon kilometres per wagon day' to judge wagon performance. The index measures:

options.A: The average distance run by wagons per day, that is, the utilisation of wagons in terms of distance
options.B: The average load carried by a wagon
options.C: The number of wagons repaired per day
options.D: The earnings per wagon per day

e: Wagon kilometres per wagon day gives the average distance run by wagons per day; it is a distance-based measure of wagon utilisation, not of load, repairs or earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In railway statistics, one traffic unit represents one passenger kilometre or one Net Tonne Kilometre of goods traffic.
2. Earnings per traffic unit are worked out by dividing the gross earnings of the railway by the total traffic units performed by it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: one traffic unit is one passenger kilometre or one Net Tonne Kilometre of goods traffic, and earnings per traffic unit = gross earnings divided by the total traffic units performed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Monthly Statistical Statement 3-A is concerned with the performance of passenger and goods trains, covering tonne kilometres and the indices based on them.
2. Monthly Statistical Statement 6-B relates to parcel traffic statistics.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Monthly Statistical Statement 3-A covers the performance of passenger and goods trains, including tonne kilometres and the indices based on them, and Monthly Statistical Statement 6-B relates to parcel traffic statistics.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In goods traffic statistics, traffic is classified commodity-wise primarily in order to study the pattern and composition of goods traffic and its trends.
2. Monthly Statistical Statement 7-C gives particulars of tonnes originating, transhipped and terminating for the major commodities.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: goods traffic is classified commodity-wise to study its pattern, composition and trends, and Monthly Statistical Statement 7-C gives tonnes originating, transhipped and terminating for the major commodities.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Train Enquiry System primarily provides real-time information about the running of trains for the travelling public.
2. The Control Office Application is used for real-time charting and monitoring of train movements by the operating control organisation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the National Train Enquiry System gives the public real-time train running information, and the Control Office Application is used by the operating control organisation for real-time charting and monitoring of train movements.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The abbreviation TAMS, used in the Traffic Accounts Offices, stands for Traffic Accounts Management System.
2. Under TAMS, every modification in the station data is routed through the Error Sheet module, so that accountal and traceability are ensured.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: TAMS stands for Traffic Accounts Management System, and under it every modification in station data is routed through the Error Sheet module so that accountal and traceability are ensured.

q: The Traffic Accounts Office has to work out the shares of two railways in the earnings of a through goods consignment. The apportionment of earnings of through goods traffic among the railways is worked out primarily on the basis of:

options.A: The number of stations on each railway
options.B: The staff strength of each railway
options.D: The abstracts of invoices and earnings exchanged between the railways concerned

e: Apportionment of through goods earnings between railways is worked out in the Traffic Accounts Office primarily from the abstracts of invoices and earnings exchanged between the railways concerned, on the basis of the distance carried over each railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Coaching earnings of a railway comprise passenger earnings and other coaching earnings.
2. Within coaching earnings, passenger earnings are further classified as suburban and non-suburban earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: coaching earnings comprise passenger earnings and other coaching earnings, and passenger earnings are further classified as suburban and non-suburban.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Demurrage and wharfage charges realised at stations are classified as part of goods earnings.
2. Siding charges recovered from siding owners for the services rendered in sidings are classified as part of goods earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both demurrage and wharfage realised at stations and siding charges recovered from siding owners for services rendered in sidings are classified as part of goods earnings.

q: A consignment is booked over a notified ghat section where the cost of working is high. For such specified sections, passenger fares and goods freight are charged:

options.A: On the actual distance of the section only
options.B: At double the ordinary rates on the actual distance
options.C: On the basis of an inflated distance, higher than the actual distance, as notified for the section

e: On notified ghat sections where working costs are high, fares and freight are charged on an inflated distance, higher than the actual distance, as notified for the section, instead of on the actual distance alone.

q: Coal is carried for the Railways' own use as departmental traffic. In regard to its treatment in statistics and earnings, the correct position is that:

options.A: It is excluded from the Net Tonne Kilometres performed, but it yields goods earnings
options.B: It is included in goods earnings, but it is excluded from the Net Tonne Kilometres performed
options.C: It is excluded both from the Net Tonne Kilometres performed and from goods earnings
options.D: It is included in the Net Tonne Kilometres performed, but goods earnings arise only from commercial traffic and not from departmental traffic

e: Departmental traffic such as coal carried for the Railways' own use is included in the Net Tonne Kilometres performed, but it yields no goods earnings, because goods earnings arise only from commercial traffic.

q: At a Private Freight Terminal, a customer asks who will load and unload his traffic. The correct position at such a terminal is that:

options.A: Loading, unloading and terminal handling are done by the terminal operator, while the Railways provide the rail movement and recover the freight and terminal charges
options.B: All loading, unloading and handling is done by railway staff only
options.C: No freight is recovered by the Railways for traffic handled at the terminal
options.D: The terminal can be used only for container traffic

e: At a Private Freight Terminal, loading, unloading and terminal handling are done by the terminal operator, while the Railways provide the rail movement and recover the freight and the prescribed terminal charges.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Automobile Freight Train Operator scheme, private operators invest in specially designed wagons for the carriage of automobiles, on payment of haulage charges to the Railways.
2. Under the Wagon Leasing Scheme, wagons can be procured on lease from wagon leasing companies by end users and operators for freight movement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both schemes are correctly described: under the Automobile Freight Train Operator scheme private operators invest in special automobile wagons and pay haulage charges, and under the Wagon Leasing Scheme wagons can be leased from wagon leasing companies by end users and operators.

q: A newly posted clerk asks what the traffic Cash Office is primarily responsible for. The correct answer is that it is responsible for:

options.C: Receiving remittances from stations, depositing the cash into the bank and accounting for the same

e: The traffic Cash Office is primarily responsible for receiving remittances from stations, depositing the cash into the bank and accounting for the same; statistics compilation and refund sanction lie elsewhere.

q: A station has remitted cash to the Cash Office and now wants to take credit for the remittance in its Balance Sheet. The credit is taken on the authority of:

options.A: The inspection note of the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.B: The station's own copy of the remittance note, without any acknowledgement
options.C: The oral confirmation of the Cashier of the Cash Office
options.D: The foil of the Cash Remittance Note returned by the Cash Office, signed by the Cashier and the Cash Witness, as an acknowledgement of the cash received

e: A station takes credit for a cash remittance on the authority of the foil of the Cash Remittance Note returned by the Cash Office, signed by the Cashier and the Cash Witness as acknowledgement of the cash received.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Claims Tribunal has been set up under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987.
2. The functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal, which dealt with complaints regarding the reasonableness of rates, now vest in the Railway Claims Tribunal.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Railway Claims Tribunal was set up under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987, and the functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal regarding reasonableness of rates now vest in it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An appeal against an order of the Railway Claims Tribunal lies to the High Court.
2. Under Section 128 of the Railways Act, 1989, a person entitled to compensation for death or injury in a train accident cannot claim compensation more than once in respect of the same accident.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: an appeal against an order of the Railway Claims Tribunal lies to the High Court, and Section 128 of the Railways Act, 1989 bars claiming compensation more than once for death or injury in the same accident.

q: Two compensation claims come up together: one for a passenger killed in a collision involving a passenger train, and the other for a passenger injured in an untoward incident. The sections of the Railways Act, 1989 under which the two claims respectively arise are:

options.A: Section 124A for the train accident claim and Section 124 for the untoward incident claim
options.C: Section 124 for the train accident claim and Section 124A for the untoward incident claim

e: Compensation for death or injury in a train accident (such as a collision involving a passenger train) arises under Section 124, while compensation for an untoward incident arises under Section 124A of the Railways Act, 1989.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Claims Tribunal consists of a Chairman and such number of Vice-Chairmen and Judicial and Technical Members as may be appointed.
2. In deciding the claims before it, the Railway Claims Tribunal is not bound by the procedure of the Code of Civil Procedure, but is guided by the principles of natural justice.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the Railway Claims Tribunal consists of a Chairman and such Vice-Chairmen and Judicial and Technical Members as may be appointed, and it is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure but is guided by the principles of natural justice.

q: A reportable train accident takes place midway between two stations. Under the Rules framed under Section 113 of the Railways Act, 1989, the first notice of the accident is to be sent by the:

options.A: Station Master nearest to the place where the accident occurred
options.B: Station Master of the destination station of the train
options.C: Travelling Ticket Examiner of the train
options.D: Chief Claims Officer of the zonal railway

e: Under the rules framed under Section 113 of the Railways Act, 1989, the first notice of a reportable train accident is sent by the Station Master nearest to the place where the accident occurred.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Passenger fares for a train journey are charged on the basis of the distance by the route by which the train actually travels.
2. For the same class and for the same distance, the fare charged for travel by a Mail or Express train is higher than the fare by an ordinary passenger train.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: fares are charged on the distance by the route by which the train actually travels, and for the same class and distance a Mail or Express fare is higher than the fare by an ordinary passenger train.

q: An accounts officer distributes the annual earnings budget of a railway over the twelve months of the year as budget proportions. The correct basis of this distribution is that:

options.A: Every month is allotted a uniform one-twelfth of the annual earnings budget
options.B: The proportions are fixed by each station for its own earnings
options.C: The budget proportions take into account the seasonal pattern of traffic over the months of the year
options.D: The whole budget is allotted to the first month and adjusted at the end of the year

e: Budget proportions distribute the annual earnings budget over the twelve months taking into account the seasonal pattern of traffic, not as a uniform one-twelfth for every month.

q: After the reservation chart of a train has been prepared, one passenger holding a ticket issued at a computerised reservation counter and another holding an e-ticket both seek cancellation and refund at the station. The correct position is that:

options.A: Neither ticket can be cancelled and no refund is admissible in either case
options.B: The e-ticket can be cancelled at the station, while the counter ticket can be dealt with only through a Ticket Deposit Receipt
options.C: Both tickets can be cancelled at the station on the same terms
options.D: The counter ticket can be cancelled at the station subject to the prescribed time limits, while the e-ticket cannot be cancelled after chart preparation and refund, where admissible, can only be claimed by filing a Ticket Deposit Receipt

e: After chart preparation, a counter (PRS) ticket can still be cancelled at the station within the prescribed time limits, but an e-ticket cannot be cancelled after chart preparation; refund, where admissible, is claimed only by filing a Ticket Deposit Receipt.

q: A passenger at a computerised reservation centre in one city wants accommodation in a train which starts from a station in another city. Under the Passenger Reservation System, the correct position is that:

options.A: A passenger can reserve accommodation in any train from any computerised reservation centre, irrespective of the station from which the train starts
options.B: Reservation can be made only at the station from which the train originates
options.C: Reservation centres of one zonal railway cannot book trains of another zonal railway
options.D: Reservation is possible only through the internet and not at counters

e: Under the Passenger Reservation System, accommodation in any train can be reserved from any computerised reservation centre, irrespective of the station from which the train starts or the railway to which it belongs.

q: During a journey, a passenger asks the Travelling Ticket Examiner to allot him vacant accommodation of a higher class in the same train. The Examiner can do so:

options.A: Free of charge in all cases
options.B: Only after the train reaches its destination
options.C: Subject to availability, on payment of the difference of fare
options.D: Not at all, as upgradation is never permitted on a train

e: The Travelling Ticket Examiner may allot vacant accommodation of a higher class in the same train during the journey, subject to availability, on payment of the difference of fare between the two classes.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A passenger may get the journey on his reserved ticket postponed once to a later date, subject to the prescribed conditions, availability of accommodation and charges.
2. A passenger holding a reserved ticket can get the boarding station changed, on request made before the departure of the train, subject to the prescribed conditions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both facilities exist under the reservation rules: a journey on a reserved ticket may be postponed once to a later date subject to conditions, availability and charges, and the boarding station can be changed on request made before the train's departure.
